questions.question: Which of the following is NOT the role of Food Corporation of India?

options.text: Ensuring that farmers are not forced to sell their produce below MSP
Making laws related to agricultural credit and indebtedness
Setting up purchase centres to buy produce from the farmers

questions.solution:
Option __**2**__ is NOT correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** 

 
• The Food Corporation of India is an organisation under the government of India.
 
• It was set up under the** food corporation's act in 1964.**
 
• The key objectives of the Food Corporation of India are:
 
 
• **Ensuring that farmers are not forced to sell their produce below MSP** by providing effective price support operations.
 
• **Setting up purchase centers to buy produce from the farmers.**
 
• Distribution of foodgrains throughout the country for the public distribution system.
 
• **Maintaining a satisfactory level of operational and buffer stocks of foodgrains** to ensure National Food Security.
 
• To intervene in the market for price stabilization.
 
 
 
• The headquarters of the food corporation of India is in **New Delhi.**
 
• **Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food, and Public Distribution** is the parent organisation of the food corporation of India.

questions.question: Which part protects an unopened flower?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sepals**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• **Sepals** protect an unopened flower

 
 
• Sepals are green, leaf-like structures that protect the flower in the **bud stage.**
 
• Sepals are collectively called the **calyx.**
 
• Sepals most resemble leaves due to their green color.
 
• Sepals may be brightly colored and function as petals when true petals are missing.
 
 
• **Virgin’s bower and the Bougainvillea **are examples of Sepals functioned as petals.
 
 
 
• The number of petals will be the same as the number of sepals in most cases. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Petals **are brightly colored parts of a flower that helps to attract insects for pollination. 
 
• **Stamen** is the male reproductive organ of a flower.
 
• **The anther **is the part of a stamen that contains the pollen.

 [IMAGE: https://letstalkscience.ca/sites/default/files/2020-06/parts_of_a_flower.png]

questions.question: When did the Indian Constituent assembly adopt the constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 26 November 1949.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• The Constituent Assembly adopted the Indian Constitution on **November 26, 1949**.
 
• The Indian National Congress made the demand for a constituent assembly in **1934**.
 
• The Constitution of India was officially framed by the Constituent Assembly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The constituent assembly was set up on **December 6, 1946**.

 
 
• It was constituted under the provisions of the **Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946**.
 
 
 
• The first official meeting of the constituent assembly was held on **December 9, 1946**.
 
• **Sachidananda Sinha** was appointed as the temporary chairman during its first meeting.
 
• **Dr. Rajendra Prasad** was elected as the permanent president of the constituent assembly on** December 11, 1946**.
 
• The Constituent Assembly also appointed** H.C. Mukherjee** as its vice president.
 
• The constitutional advisor to the constituent assembly was **B. N. Rao**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **Mistake Points__**

__
 
• The Constitution of India came into being on **January 26, 1950**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The constituent assembly adopted the national flag on** July 22, 1947.**
 
• The constituent assembly adopted the national anthem on **January 24, 1950**.
 
• The constituent assembly adopted the national song on **January 24, 1950**.

questions.question: Out of the given options, which crop grows in black soil?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cotton.**__

__
 
• Out of the given options, only cotton crops grow in black soil.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

__
 
• Black soil is also called as ‘**Regur Soil’** or the ‘**Black Cotton Soil**’.
 
• Black soil is well suited for the **cultivation of cotton** so it is also called cotton soil.
 
• The black soils are generally clayey, deep, and impermeable.
 
• Blach soils are formed by the disintegration of** basalt.**
 
• Black soil has the ability to retain moisture for a very long time.
 
• Black soils are rich in soil nutrients, such as calcium carbonate, magnesium, and potash.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Alluvial soil is suitable for the growth of **sugarcane**, paddy, wheat, and other cereal and pulse crops.
 
• Laterite soil is very useful for growing** tea**, coffee, and **cashew nut.**

questions.question: Name the bacteria that causes dysentery.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Shigella.__

__
 
• Dysentery is an infection of the intestines that causes diarrhea containing blood.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Dysentery is caused by shigella bacteria.

 
 
• It is spread by contaminated water and food
 
• Dysentery caused by Shigella is also called as Bacillary dysentery or shigellosis.
 
• Shigella is a rod-shaped bacteria under the Enterobacteriaceae family.
 
• Shigella is genetically closely related to E. coli.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **Mistake Points__**

__
 
• Dysentery can be **caused by bacteria as well as protozoa**.
 
• The dysentery caused by protozoa is called **amoebic dysentery or amoebiasis** because the causative organism is ***Entamoeba histolytica***.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Cholerae is the disease caused by the Vibrio cholera bacteria.
 
• Tuberculosis is the disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis bacteria.
 
• Diseases like rheumatic fever, impetigo, scarlet fever, puerperal fever are caused by Streptococcus pyogenes bacteria.

questions.question: Liquefied petroleum gas consists of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Propane and butane**__.

__
 
• The petroleum gas liquefied under pressure is called liquefied petroleum gas(LPG).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• Liquefied petroleum gas consists of **propane and butane**.
 
• Liquefied petroleum gas is used as fuel for home and industry.
 
• The chemical which is added to liquefied petroleum gas(LPG) to detect leakage is **ethyl mercaptan**.
 
• Liquefied petroleum gas used for domestic applications in cylinders under relatively low pressures.
 
• Liquefied petroleum gas can be stored nearly indefinitely without degradation. 
 
• The molecular formula of butane is** C₄H₁₀**.
 
• The molecular formula of propane is **C₃H₈**.

questions.question: Which schedule was added to the Indian Constitution in 1992 as a result of the 73rd amendment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**11th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** 

__
 
• The 73rd amendment in 1992 added a new **eleventh schedule** to the Indian constitution.

 
 
• The eleventh schedule specifies the power, authority, and responsibilities of **Panchayats.**
 
• **Twenty-nine subjects** are listed in the eleventh schedule of the Constitution.
 
• These subjects are to be transferred to the Panchayati Raj institutions.
 
 
 
• The 73rd amendment act is also called as "**Panchayati raj act**".
 
 
• The 73rd amendment act has added a new **Part IX** to the constitution of India.
 
• It consists of provisions from article **243 to 243 O.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The eighth schedule** consists of the 22 languages, recognized by the Indian constitution.
 
• The **ninth** schedule consists of the acts and regulations of the state legislature dealing with land reforms and the abolition of the zamindari system.
 
• The 74th amendment in 1992 added a new **twelfth schedule **to the Indian constitution.

questions.question: .......... is a chemical process or a reaction between fuel (hydrocarbon) and oxygen producing heat and light energy resulting in a flame.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Combustion.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• **Combustion** is a chemical process or a reaction between a fuel (hydrocarbon) and oxygen-producing heat and light energy resulting in a flame.

 
 
• The substance that undergoes combustion is called **combustible.**
 
• The substance like carbon, candle, magnesium, sulphur are examples of combustible substances.
 
• **Air is necessary for combustion.**
 
• A combustible substance cannot catch fire or burn as long as its temperature is lower than its ignition temperature.
 
• Phosphorus which burns in air at room temperature is an example of **spontaneous combustion.**
 
• The combustion of most fuels releases **carbon dioxide** in the environment.
 
• The incomplete combustion of fuel gives poisonous** carbon monoxide** gas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Convection** is a mode of heat transfer by actual motion of matter either by natural or forced.
 
• The slow process of conversion of dead vegetation into coal is called **carbonisation.**
 
• **Conduction** is the process of transfer of heat between two adjacent parts of a body due to their temperature difference.
